title: Timers and journal evidence
subtitle: Schedule repeatable work with systemd timers and read the journal like an operator instead of guessing.
objectives: Choose between a timer and a cron job
Pair a timer unit with a service unit
Express a schedule with OnCalendar and Persistent
Use journalctl filters to find a unit’s evidence

ex200.evidence: Explain systemd timer integration with journald and dependencies.
Use OnCalendar and Persistent in a timer unit.

versionNotes: RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 both support systemd timers, OnCalendar expressions, and Persistent=true. Newer systemd versions may support additional calendar syntax.
journalctl is the same interface on both releases. RHEL 10 may have a different default journal size, so verify retention rather than assuming it.

lab.title: Nightly backup, visible in the journal
lab.scenario: Create a backup script, a oneshot service, and a timer that runs it every night. Enable the timer and inspect its status and logs.

steps.text: Read authentication evidence from sshd in the journal.
steps.verify: Output is filtered to sshd and includes accepted or failed login lines.

steps.text: Create the backup script and make it executable.
steps.cmd: printf "#!/bin/bash\necho backup \$(date)\n" | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/fieldbook-backup && sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/fieldbook-backup
steps.verify: The script exists with execute permission.

steps.text: Create the oneshot service that the timer will trigger.
steps.verify: The service has an absolute ExecStart and runs as a oneshot.

steps.text: Create a timer with a nightly calendar schedule and persistence.
steps.cmd:
printf "[Unit]
Description=Run fieldbook backup nightly

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:00:00
Persistent=true
Unit=fieldbook-backup.service

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
" | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/fieldbook-backup.timer
steps.verify: The timer names the service, uses OnCalendar, and installs into timers.target.

steps.text: Reload, enable the timer, and confirm the next trigger.
steps.cmd: sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now fieldbook-backup.timer && systemctl list-timers --all
steps.verify: fieldbook-backup.timer is enabled and appears in the timer list.

steps.text: Inspect timer status and service journal evidence.
steps.verify: Status shows the timer and the journal command is filtered to the paired service.

quiz.q: Which pair correctly schedules a oneshot job?
options: A timer and a matching service
quiz.why: A timer triggers a unit, normally a oneshot service with the same base name.

quiz.q: What does Persistent=true do on a timer?
options: Triggers a missed run after boot
quiz.why: Persistent tells systemd to account for time the machine was off and run a missed job once.

quiz.q: Which command shows only sshd journal entries without a pager?
quiz.why: -u filters by unit and --no-pager writes the full output to the terminal.
